panels.title: Hardened Dockerfile pattern
panels.body:
FROM node:20-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY . .

FROM gcr.io/distroless/nodejs20-debian12
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app .
USER nonroot          # distroless ships a 'nonroot' user (UID 65532)
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["server.js"]

panels.title: Capability escape — most common container breakout vector
panels.body:
Default Docker container has 14 capabilities.
CAP_NET_ADMIN lets container modify host routing tables.
CAP_SYS_ADMIN is near-root — can mount filesystems, ptrace.
privileged: true disables ALL capability dropping — same as root on host.

Hardened runtime flags:
  --cap-drop ALL
  --cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE   # only if port < 1024 needed
  --read-only                  # read-only root filesystem
  --no-new-privileges          # blocks setuid/setgid escalation
  --security-opt seccomp=profile.json
  --security-opt no-new-privileges

panels.title: Rootless Docker vs root Docker
pros: Rootless: daemon runs as unprivileged user; container breakout = unprivileged access, not root
Rootless: user namespace maps container root (UID 0) to a high host UID (e.g. 100000)
cons: Rootless: some features unavailable — AppArmor profiles, overlay storage on older kernels, some network modes
Root Docker: full feature set; acceptable with --cap-drop ALL + seccomp + read-only rootfs defense-in-depth
